add_variable_mode.description: Add a new mode to an existing variable collection (e.g. Light/Dark, Desktop/Mobile). IMPORTANT — Figma free plan only allows 1 mode per collection; calling this tool on a free-plan account will return the error 'Limited to 1 modes only'. If that error occurs, stop retrying and switch to the name-prefix workaround: keep the single default mode and create variables prefixed by mode, e.g. 'light/color-bg' and 'dark/color-bg' in the same collection. Tell the user that native multi-mode variables require a paid Figma plan (Professional or above).
add_variable_mode.name: add_variable_mode

apply_style_to_node.description: Apply an existing local style (paint, text, effect, or grid) to a node, linking the node to that style.

nodeId.description: Target node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

target.description: For paint styles only — apply to 'fill' (default) or 'stroke'

apply_style_to_node.name: apply_style_to_node

batch_execute_pipeline.description: Execute a batch pipeline of mutation steps in Figma, passing values between steps via $variables. On failure with stop_on_error, rollback removes nodes the pipeline created and restores properties it changed on existing nodes (position, size, fills, strokes, opacity, visibility, name, text, blend mode, constraints). Rollback CANNOT undo deletions (delete_nodes, delete_page), structural changes (group/ungroup, detach_instance, reparent), or steps that target a node by name instead of id.

steps.description: Array of pipeline steps to execute in sequence. Each step is {id, action, params, export_vars?}.

action.description: Tool name to run e.g. create_frame

export_vars.description: Map of variable name to a field of this step's result

id.description: Step identifier, referenced by $variables in later steps

stop_on_error.description: Whether to stop execution and rollback on error (default true)

batch_execute_pipeline.name: batch_execute_pipeline

batch_rename_nodes.description: Rename one or more nodes: pass `name` to set the name outright, or find/replace, regex substitution, or prefix/suffix to derive it from the current one. `name` cannot be combined with the others — a literal name and a substitution in the same call have no defined order.

find.description: String (or regex pattern when useRegex=true) to search for in the node name

name.description: New name, applied as given to every node listed. Figma supports slash-separated path notation e.g. 'Icons/Arrow/Left' to organise nodes in component panels.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

prefix.description: String to prepend to the node name

regexFlags.description: Regex flags e.g. 'gi' (default 'g'). Only used when useRegex=true.

replace.description: Replacement string. Required when find is provided.

suffix.description: String to append to the node name

useRegex.description: Treat find as a regular expression (default false)

batch_rename_nodes.name: batch_rename_nodes

bind_variable_to_node.description: Bind a local variable to a node property so the property is driven by the variable's value. COLOR variables: use fillColor or strokeColor. BOOLEAN variables: use visible. FLOAT variables: use opacity, rotation, width, height, cornerRadius, topLeftRadius, topRightRadius, bottomLeftRadius, bottomRightRadius, strokeWeight, itemSpacing, paddingTop, paddingRight, paddingBottom, paddingLeft.

field.description: Property to bind: fillColor | strokeColor | visible | opacity | rotation | width | height | cornerRadius | topLeftRadius | topRightRadius | bottomLeftRadius | bottomRightRadius | strokeWeight | itemSpacing | paddingTop | paddingRight | paddingBottom | paddingLeft

nodeId.description: Target node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

bind_variable_to_node.name: bind_variable_to_node

boolean_operation.description: Combine two or more shapes into one: UNION merges them, SUBTRACT cuts the later shapes out of the first, INTERSECT keeps the overlap, EXCLUDE keeps everything but the overlap. Node order is meaningful for SUBTRACT and EXCLUDE. All nodes must share a parent. This consumes the shapes and cannot be rolled back by a pipeline — call save_version_checkpoint first if the shapes matter.

nodeIds.description: Shape node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345', '4029:12346']; for SUBTRACT and EXCLUDE the first is the shape the others are cut from

boolean_operation.name: boolean_operation

clone_node.description: Clone an existing node, optionally repositioning it or placing it in a new parent.

nodeId.description: Source node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

parentId.description: Parent node ID for the clone. Defaults to same parent as source.

clone_node.name: clone_node

combine_as_variants.description: Combine two or more COMPONENT nodes into a single COMPONENT_SET, so they become variants of one component. The components must already share a parent. Add VARIANT properties afterwards with manage_component_properties to say what distinguishes them.

name.description: Name for the resulting component set

nodeIds.description: COMPONENT node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345', '4029:12346']

combine_as_variants.name: combine_as_variants

create_component.description: Convert an existing FRAME node into a reusable COMPONENT. The frame is replaced in place by the new component.

name.description: Optional name for the component. Defaults to the frame's current name.

nodeId.description: FRAME node ID to convert, in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

create_component.name: create_component

create_component_instance.description: Create an instance of a Component. If the target is a ComponentSet (Variant Set), it automatically instantiates the default variant. It can instantiate local components or library components (using componentKey).

componentId.description: ID of the local component or component set in colon format e.g. 4029:12345. Preferred over componentKey if available.

componentKey.description: Key of a component from a Team Library to import and instantiate.

parentId.description: Optional. Parent node ID to place the instance inside. If missing, places it on the current page.

x.description: Optional. X coordinate. If missing, it will be centered in the viewport.

create_component_instance.name: create_component_instance

create_connector.description: Create a Connector line in FigJam. NOTE: Only works in FigJam files!

endNodeId.description: Optional. End node ID in colon format e.g. 2:2

startNodeId.description: Optional. Start node ID in colon format e.g. 1:1

create_connector.name: create_connector

create_node.description: Create a shape on the current page or inside a parent. `type` selects which, and each takes its own arguments — FRAME: width, height, fillColor, and the auto-layout arguments. RECTANGLE: width, height, fillColor, cornerRadius. ELLIPSE: width, height, fillColor, startAngle, endAngle, innerRadiusRatio (the last three make arcs and rings). STAR: pointCount, outerRadius, innerRadius, fillColor, cornerRadius. POLYGON: pointCount, radius, fillColor, cornerRadius. LINE: length, rotation, strokeColor, strokeWeight. SECTION: width, height — and no parent, sections live on the page. x, y and name apply to all of them. An argument belonging to a different shape is rejected rather than ignored. Use create_text for text and create_component_instance for components.

clipsContent.description: Clip children to the frame's bounds

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels. RECTANGLE, STAR, POLYGON.

counterAxisAlignItems.description: Cross-axis alignment: MIN, CENTER, MAX, or BASELINE

counterAxisSpacing.description: Gap between wrapped rows/columns (only when layoutWrap is WRAP)

endAngle.description: ELLIPSE: arc end angle in radians (default a full turn)

fillColor.description: Fill color as hex e.g. #FF5733. Every shape but LINE and SECTION.

height.description: Height in pixels (default 100). FRAME, RECTANGLE, ELLIPSE, SECTION.

innerRadius.description: STAR: inner radius in pixels (default 0.3819 of the outer)

innerRadiusRatio.description: ELLIPSE: inner radius as a fraction of the outer, for rings and donuts (default 0)

itemReverseZIndex.description: Stack children last-on-top instead of first-on-top

layoutAlign.description: Cross-axis alignment of this node within its PARENT's auto layout

layoutGrow.description: Whether this node grows along its PARENT's main axis: 0 to keep its size, 1 to fill the free space

layoutMode.description: Auto-layout direction: HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, or NONE

layoutPositioning.description: How this node sits in its PARENT's auto layout: AUTO to flow with its siblings, ABSOLUTE to float free of them at its own x/y

layoutSizingHorizontal.description: Horizontal sizing: FIXED, HUG (shrink to contents), or FILL (fill the parent). Prefer this over counterAxisSizingMode/primaryAxisSizingMode — it is the only way to express 'fill container'. HUG needs auto-layout on this node; FILL needs auto-layout on its parent.

layoutSizingVertical.description: Vertical sizing: FIXED, HUG (shrink to contents), or FILL (fill the parent). Same requirements as layoutSizingHorizontal.

maxHeight.description: Maximum height in pixels; pass null to clear it

maxWidth.description: Maximum width in pixels; pass null to clear it

minHeight.description: Minimum height in pixels; pass null to clear it

minWidth.description: Minimum width in pixels; pass null to clear it

name.description: Node name shown in the layers panel

parentId.description: Parent node ID in colon format. Defaults to current page. Not accepted for SECTION.

pointCount.description: STAR: number of points (default 5). POLYGON: number of sides (default 3).

primaryAxisAlignItems.description: Main-axis alignment: MIN, CENTER, MAX, or SPACE_BETWEEN

startAngle.description: ELLIPSE: arc start angle in radians (default 0)

strokeColor.description: LINE: stroke color as hex e.g. #000000

strokesIncludedInLayout.description: Count this node's stroke width as part of the layout size

type.description: Shape to create: FRAME, RECTANGLE, ELLIPSE, STAR, POLYGON, LINE, or SECTION

width.description: Width in pixels (default 100). FRAME, RECTANGLE, ELLIPSE, SECTION.

create_node.name: create_node

create_style.description: Create a local style. `type` selects what kind, and each kind takes its own arguments — PAINT: color. TEXT: fontSize, fontFamily, fontStyle, textDecoration, lineHeightValue/Unit, letterSpacingValue/Unit. EFFECT: effectType, color, opacity, radius, offsetX, offsetY, spread. GRID: pattern, count, gutterSize, offset, alignment, sectionSize, color, opacity. An argument belonging to a different kind is rejected rather than ignored. Returns the new style's ID; apply it with apply_style_to_node.

alignment.description: GRID: STRETCH (default), CENTER, MIN, or MAX (COLUMNS/ROWS only)

color.description: PAINT: fill color as hex e.g. #FF5733 (required). EFFECT: shadow color (default #000000). GRID: grid line color (default #FF0000)

count.description: GRID: number of columns or rows (COLUMNS/ROWS only, default 12)

description.description: Optional description shown in the Figma style panel

effectType.description: EFFECT: DROP_SHADOW (default), INNER_SHADOW, LAYER_BLUR, or BACKGROUND_BLUR

fontFamily.description: TEXT: font family name e.g. 'Inter', 'Roboto' (default Inter). Must be installed in Figma.

gutterSize.description: GRID: gutter size in pixels (COLUMNS/ROWS only, default 16)

letterSpacingUnit.description: TEXT: letter spacing unit — PIXELS (default) or PERCENT

letterSpacingValue.description: TEXT: letter spacing value (unit set by letterSpacingUnit)

lineHeightUnit.description: TEXT: line height unit — PIXELS (default) or PERCENT

lineHeightValue.description: TEXT: line height value (unit set by lineHeightUnit)

name.description: Style name — use slash notation to organise into groups e.g. 'Brand/Primary', 'Heading/H1'

offset.description: GRID: margin in pixels (COLUMNS/ROWS only, default 0)

offsetX.description: EFFECT: shadow X offset in pixels (default 0)

offsetY.description: EFFECT: shadow Y offset in pixels (default 4)

opacity.description: EFFECT: shadow color opacity 0–1 (default 0.25). GRID: grid line opacity 0–1 (default 0.1)

pattern.description: GRID: pattern — GRID (default), COLUMNS, or ROWS

radius.description: EFFECT: blur radius in pixels (default 8 for shadows, 4 for blurs)

sectionSize.description: GRID: cell size in pixels (GRID pattern only, default 8)

type.description: Kind of style: PAINT, TEXT, EFFECT, or GRID

create_style.name: create_style

create_text.description: Create a new text node on the current page or inside a parent node. The font is loaded automatically before insertion. Returns the created node ID and bounds. Use set_text to update the content of an existing text node.

fillColor.description: Text color as hex e.g. #000000 (default black)

fontFamily.description: Font family name e.g. 'Inter', 'Roboto', 'SF Pro Display' (default Inter). Must be a font installed in Figma.

fontStyle.description: Font style variant e.g. 'Regular', 'Bold', 'Italic', 'Medium', 'SemiBold' (default Regular). Must match an available style for the chosen fontFamily.

name.description: Node name shown in the layers panel (defaults to the text content)

parentId.description: Parent node ID in colon format. Defaults to current page.

create_text.name: create_text

create_variable.description: Create a new variable (design token) inside an existing collection. Returns the new variable's ID. Use get_variable_defs to find collection IDs, set_variable_value to set values per mode, and bind_variable_to_node to apply the variable to a node property.

collectionId.description: ID of the variable collection to add this variable to (from get_variable_defs)

name.description: Variable name — use slash notation to group e.g. 'Color/Primary', 'Spacing/MD'

type.description: Variable type: COLOR (hex color), FLOAT (numeric dimension/spacing), STRING (text), or BOOLEAN (true/false toggle)

value.description: Initial value for the first mode. COLOR: hex e.g. #FF5733. FLOAT: number e.g. 16. STRING: text. BOOLEAN: true or false.

create_variable.name: create_variable

create_variable_collection.description: Create a new local variable collection with an optional initial mode name. NOTE — Figma free plan limits each collection to 1 mode. If you need Light/Dark (or any multi-mode) theming and the user is on the free plan, do NOT try to call add_variable_mode; instead use the name-prefix workaround: create all variables in a single collection and prefix each variable name with its mode, e.g. 'light/color-bg' and 'dark/color-bg'. Inform the user of this limitation.
create_variable_collection.name: create_variable_collection

create_vector.description: Create a vector node from SVG markup — the way to bring in an icon. An SVG with a single path becomes the vector itself; one with several becomes a frame containing them. Returns the created node ID and bounds.

fillColor.description: Override the fill colour as hex e.g. '#FF5733'

height.description: Resize the result to this height

parentId.description: Parent node ID to insert into, colon format e.g. '4029:99' (default: current page)

svg.description: SVG markup e.g. '<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 2 L22 22 L2 22 Z"/></svg>'

width.description: Resize the result to this width

create_vector.name: create_vector

delete_nodes.description: Delete one or more nodes. This cannot be undone via MCP — use with care.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to delete in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

delete_nodes.name: delete_nodes

delete_style.description: Delete a style (paint, text, effect, or grid) by its ID.
delete_style.name: delete_style

delete_variable.description: Delete a single variable (provide variableId) or an entire collection and all its variables (provide collectionId). Provide exactly one of the two — not both.

collectionId.description: Collection ID to delete (removes all variables in the collection)

delete_variable.name: delete_variable

detach_instance.description: Detach one or more component instances, converting them to plain frames. The link to the main component is broken; all visual properties are preserved.

nodeIds.description: INSTANCE node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

detach_instance.name: detach_instance

export_frames_to_pdf.description: Export multiple frames as a single multi-page PDF file. Each frame becomes one page in order. Ideal for pitch decks, proposals, and slide exports.

nodeIds.description: Ordered list of frame node IDs to export as PDF pages, colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

outputPath.description: File path to write the PDF to, must end in .pdf (relative to working directory or absolute)

export_frames_to_pdf.name: export_frames_to_pdf

export_tokens.description: Export all design tokens (variables and paint styles) as JSON or CSS custom properties. Ideal for bridging Figma variables into your codebase.
export_tokens.name: export_tokens

find_replace_text.description: Find and replace text content across all TEXT nodes in a subtree. Searches the entire current page if no nodeId is given.

find.description: Text string (or regex pattern when useRegex=true) to search for

nodeId.description: Root node ID to scope the search. Defaults to the entire current page.

regexFlags.description: Regex flags e.g. 'gi' (default 'g'). Only used when useRegex=true.

replace.description: Replacement string (use empty string to delete matches)

useRegex.description: Treat find as a regular expression (default false)

find_replace_text.name: find_replace_text

flatten_nodes.description: Flatten nodes into a single vector, merging their geometry and discarding the layer structure. Use it to simplify a finished icon. All nodes must share a parent. This consumes the nodes and cannot be rolled back by a pipeline.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to flatten in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

flatten_nodes.name: flatten_nodes

get_annotations.description: Get dev-mode annotations in the current document or scoped to a specific node. Returns annotation objects with label text, measurement type, and the ID of the annotated node. Omit nodeId to retrieve all annotations on the current page.

nodeId.description: Optional — scope results to annotations on this node and its descendants, colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

get_annotations.name: get_annotations

get_design_context.description: Get a depth-limited, token-efficient tree of the current selection or page. Use this instead of get_document when exploring large files. Supports detail levels (minimal/compact/full) and dedupe_components for pages heavy with repeated component instances.

dedupe_components.description: When true, INSTANCE nodes are serialized compactly (mainComponentId + componentProperties + overrides array of differing text/nested content) and unique component definitions are collected once in a top-level componentDefs map. Highly token-efficient for screens with many repeated component instances.

depth.description: How many levels deep to traverse (default 2)

detail.description: Property verbosity: minimal (id/name/type/bounds only), compact (+fills/strokes/opacity), full (everything, default)

get_design_context.name: get_design_context

get_document.description: Get the node tree of the current page, or of every page with scope 'document'. Unbounded by default and can be very large; pass depth or maxNodes to cap it. A capped result sets `truncated`, and every node whose children were withheld reports `childCount` and `childrenOmitted`, so a short answer is never mistaken for a whole one. Prefer get_design_context for exploration or when token efficiency matters.

depth.description: How many levels below the page to walk. 0 returns the page alone. Omit for no limit.

maxNodes.description: Stop after this many nodes, walking in tree order so the result is the same every time. Omit for no limit.

scope.description: 'page' (default) walks the current page. 'document' walks every page in the file, sharing one depth/maxNodes budget across them and reporting each page as a child of the document.

get_document.name: get_document

get_fonts.description: List all fonts used in the current page, sorted by usage frequency. Useful for understanding typography without scanning all text nodes.
get_fonts.name: get_fonts

get_image_bytes.description: Read the original bytes of the images placed on nodes, as base64. This is the asset that was imported, not a re-render — use get_screenshot when you want a picture of how a node looks now. One image used on several nodes is returned once. Nodes with no image fill are reported under `skipped` rather than failing the call.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs carrying image fills, in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

get_image_bytes.name: get_image_bytes

get_instance_overrides.description: Get the component properties (variants, booleans, text) of a component instance. Includes their current values and type information. Use this before set_instance_overrides to know what properties exist.

nodeId.description: INSTANCE node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

get_instance_overrides.name: get_instance_overrides

get_local_components.description: Get all components defined in the current Figma file.
get_local_components.name: get_local_components

get_metadata.description: Get metadata about the current Figma document: file name, page count, which page is open, and every page in the file with its ID and name. Loads no node trees, so it is the cheap way to find a page ID before working on it.
get_metadata.name: get_metadata

get_nodes_info.description: Get full details for one or more nodes by ID in one round-trip. Answers {nodes: [...]}, plus a globalVars.styles map when a fill or stroke was shared by more than one node and collapsed to a ref. An ID that matches nothing is reported under `missing` rather than dropped, so a typo cannot read as a node with no content. Node IDs must use colon format e.g. '4029:12345', never hyphens.

nodeIds.description: List of node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345', '4029:67890']

get_nodes_info.name: get_nodes_info

get_reactions.description: Get the prototype reactions defined on a node. Returns an array of reaction objects — each has a trigger (e.g. ON_CLICK, ON_HOVER, AFTER_TIMEOUT) and an actions array (navigate to node, open URL, go back, etc.). Use set_reactions to add or replace reactions, remove_reactions to delete them.

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

get_reactions.name: get_reactions

get_screenshot.description: Export a screenshot of one or more nodes as base64-encoded image data (held in memory). Use save_screenshots instead when you want to write images directly to disk without base64 in the response.

format.description: Export format: PNG (default), SVG, JPG, or PDF

nodeIds.description: Optional node IDs to export, colon format. If empty, exports current selection.

get_screenshot.name: get_screenshot

get_selection.description: Get the nodes currently selected in Figma, or the set the user pinned in the plugin panel. Returns an empty array if nothing is selected or pinned. Use get_design_context or get_nodes_info to retrieve deeper detail about specific nodes by ID.

source.description: 'selection' (default) follows what is selected right now, which moves the moment the user clicks elsewhere. 'pinned' reads the set they pinned in the panel, which holds still across a conversation — prefer it when you need the same nodes over several calls.

get_selection.name: get_selection

get_styles.description: Get all local styles in the document (paint, text, effect, and grid). Returns each style's ID, name, type, and properties. Use the style ID with apply_style_to_node or update_paint_style. For design tokens (variables), use get_variable_defs instead.
get_styles.name: get_styles

get_variable_defs.description: Get all local variable definitions: collections, modes, and values. Variables are Figma's design token system.
get_variable_defs.name: get_variable_defs

get_viewport.description: Get the current Figma viewport: scroll center, zoom level, and visible bounds.
get_viewport.name: get_viewport

group_nodes.description: Group two or more nodes into a GROUP. All nodes must share the same parent.

name.description: Optional name for the new group

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to group (minimum 2), in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345', '4029:12346']

group_nodes.name: group_nodes

import_image.description: Place an image in Figma, from a URL or from base64 data. Prefer imageUrl: base64 pushes the whole file through the plugin connection, which is the expensive half of placing an image. By default the image lands as a new rectangle sized to the image itself; pass nodeId to paint it onto a node that already exists instead — an avatar or a hero slot usually does.

crop.description: Show only part of the image, as fractions of it: {x, y, width, height} from 0 to 1, where {x:0.25, y:0, width:0.5, height:1} is the middle half. Sets scaleMode to CROP.

height.description: Height as a fraction of the image height, 0-1

width.description: Width as a fraction of the image width, 0-1

x.description: Left edge as a fraction of the image width, 0-1

y.description: Top edge as a fraction of the image height, 0-1

filters.description: Image adjustments, each from -1 to 1 and 0 for no change. Omitted ones stay at 0.

height.description: Height in pixels. Omit to use the image's own size, scaled to fit 1000px.

imageData.description: Base64-encoded image data (PNG or JPG), when there is no URL to fetch

imageUrl.description: URL of the image to fetch. Preferred over imageData.

mode.description: With nodeId: replace the node's fills (default) or append the image to them

nodeId.description: Paint the image onto this existing node instead of creating a rectangle, colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

parentId.description: Parent node ID in colon format. Defaults to current page.

scaleMode.description: Image scale mode: FILL (default), FIT, CROP, or TILE

width.description: Width in pixels. Omit to use the image's own size, scaled to fit 1000px.

import_image.name: import_image

manage_component_properties.description: Define what a component exposes to its instances. `add` declares a property, `edit` renames it or changes its default, `delete` removes it, and `bind` points one of the component's own layers at a property so setting it actually does something — a BOOLEAN drives the layer's visibility, a TEXT its characters, an INSTANCE_SWAP its component. Properties may be named without the `#1:2` suffix Figma appends; the current id is resolved for you and returned. Use set_instance_overrides to set the values on an instance.

action.description: What to do: add, edit, delete, or bind

defaultValue.description: Default value, required for add: a boolean for BOOLEAN, a string for TEXT and VARIANT, a component ID for INSTANCE_SWAP

name.description: Property name. Required for add; for edit it renames the property.

nodeId.description: COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

preferredValues.description: For an INSTANCE_SWAP property: the components offered first in the picker

property.description: Which property to edit, delete, or bind — its name e.g. 'Size', or its full id e.g. 'Size#1:2'

targetNodeId.description: For bind: the layer inside the component that the property should drive, colon format e.g. '4029:99'

type.description: Property kind, required for add. VARIANT belongs to a COMPONENT_SET and is what distinguishes its members; the others belong to either.

manage_component_properties.name: manage_component_properties

manage_page.description: Add, delete, rename, or navigate to a page. `action` selects which, and each takes its own arguments — add: name, index. delete: pageId or pageName. rename: pageId or pageName, plus newName. navigate: pageId or pageName. An argument belonging to a different action is rejected rather than ignored. Use get_metadata to list page IDs and names.

action.description: What to do: add, delete, rename, or navigate

index.description: add: position to insert at (0 = first). Defaults to last.

name.description: add: name for the new page (default 'Page')

pageId.description: Page node ID in colon format e.g. '0:2' (delete, rename, navigate)

pageName.description: Exact page name, an alternative to pageId (delete, rename, navigate)

manage_page.name: manage_page

manage_plugin_data.description: Read and write your own metadata on a node, stored in the Figma file itself. Use it to remember what a later session cannot re-derive — which source file a component maps to, which nodes were generated and from what, a token binding. Values are strings; encode anything richer as JSON. Stored as shared plugin data, so it travels with the file and any teammate can read it.

action.description: get reads one key, set writes one, delete removes one, keys lists what is stored

key.description: Which entry to read, write, or remove. Required for every action but keys.

namespace.description: Namespace to read or write under (default 'figma-mcp-go'). Use another tool's namespace to read what it stored.

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

value.description: The string to store. Required when action is set.

manage_plugin_data.name: manage_plugin_data

outline_stroke.description: Convert each node's stroke into a filled vector, so the outline can be edited as a shape. Nodes with no visible stroke are reported under `skipped` rather than failing the call.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs whose strokes to outline, in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

outline_stroke.name: outline_stroke

remove_reactions.description: Remove prototype reactions from a node. Omit indices to remove all reactions. Provide a zero-based indices array to remove specific reactions (use get_reactions first to see current indices).

indices.description: Zero-based indices of reactions to remove. Omit or pass [] to remove all.

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

remove_reactions.name: remove_reactions

reparent_nodes.description: Move one or more nodes to a different parent frame, group, or section.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to move in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

parentId.description: Target parent node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:99'

reparent_nodes.name: reparent_nodes

save_screenshots.description: Export screenshots for multiple nodes and write them to the local filesystem. Returns file metadata (path, size, dimensions) — no base64 in the response. Use get_screenshot instead when you need the image data in memory.

format.description: Default export format: PNG (default), SVG, JPG, or PDF

items.description: List of {nodeId, outputPath, format?, scale?} objects

format.description: Export format: PNG, SVG, JPG, or PDF

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

outputPath.description: File path to write the image to

scale.description: Default export scale for raster formats (default 2)

save_screenshots.name: save_screenshots

save_version_checkpoint.description: Save a named version in the Figma file's version history. Use this before a large or risky change — batch_execute_pipeline's rollback lives only in the running plugin, so a named version is the only way back once the session ends. Figma design files only; FigJam and Slides have no version history.

description.description: Optional longer note about what is about to change

title.description: Name for this version, as it appears in Figma's version history e.g. 'Before the nav redesign'

save_version_checkpoint.name: save_version_checkpoint

search_nodes.description: Find nodes by name substring, by type, or both — omit query to take every node of the given types, omit types to search by name alone. Searches the current page by default; pass scope 'document' to search every page, or nodeId to search one subtree. Pass includeText to read the content of the TEXT nodes it finds, and includeHidden false to skip hidden nodes. The result reports `truncated` when the limit cut the answer short — raise `limit` when you mean to sweep a whole subtree, as it defaults to 50.

includeHidden.description: Whether hidden nodes are searched (default true). Pass false to skip a hidden node and everything under it, which is what a designer usually means by 'what is on this screen'.

includeText.description: Add characters, fontSize and fontName to every TEXT node in the answer (default false). Costs nothing on the other node types.

nodeId.description: Scope search to this subtree, colon format e.g. '4029:12345'. Overrides scope.

query.description: Name substring to match (case-insensitive). Omit to match every node, which is how you take all nodes of a type.

scope.description: Where to search when no nodeId is given: 'page' for the current page (default), or 'document' for every page in the file. Use 'document' when a node may live on another page — a page search reports nothing rather than looking there.

types.description: Filter by Figma node type e.g. ['TEXT', 'FRAME', 'COMPONENT']

search_nodes.name: search_nodes

set_annotations.description: Set Dev Mode Annotations on one or more nodes. Pass an empty annotations array to clear the ones a node already has. Every node gets the same annotations, and each reports its own outcome. Note: requires a paid Dev Mode seat.

annotations.description: Array of annotation objects. Example: [{"label": "Main Button"}]. Empty clears every annotation on the nodes.

nodeIds.description: Array of node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

set_annotations.name: set_annotations

set_auto_layout.description: Set or update auto-layout (flex) properties on frames, components, component sets, or instances. Covers the frame's own layout (direction, padding, gap, alignment) and how it sizes itself — use layoutSizingHorizontal/layoutSizingVertical for HUG and FILL, with minWidth/maxWidth/minHeight/maxHeight to bound them. layoutPositioning, layoutAlign, and layoutGrow describe how a node sits inside its parent's auto layout instead — pass several node IDs to put the same sizing on a whole row of siblings in one call. Each node reports its own outcome, so a sibling that cannot take the change does not stop the others.

clipsContent.description: Clip children to the frame's bounds

counterAxisAlignItems.description: Cross-axis alignment: MIN, CENTER, MAX, or BASELINE

counterAxisSpacing.description: Gap between wrapped rows/columns (only when layoutWrap is WRAP)

itemReverseZIndex.description: Stack children last-on-top instead of first-on-top

layoutAlign.description: Cross-axis alignment of this node within its PARENT's auto layout

layoutGrow.description: Whether this node grows along its PARENT's main axis: 0 to keep its size, 1 to fill the free space

layoutMode.description: Auto-layout direction: HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, or NONE

layoutPositioning.description: How this node sits in its PARENT's auto layout: AUTO to flow with its siblings, ABSOLUTE to float free of them at its own x/y

layoutSizingHorizontal.description: Horizontal sizing: FIXED, HUG (shrink to contents), or FILL (fill the parent). Prefer this over counterAxisSizingMode/primaryAxisSizingMode — it is the only way to express 'fill container'. HUG needs auto-layout on this node; FILL needs auto-layout on its parent.

layoutSizingVertical.description: Vertical sizing: FIXED, HUG (shrink to contents), or FILL (fill the parent). Same requirements as layoutSizingHorizontal.

maxHeight.description: Maximum height in pixels; pass null to clear it

maxWidth.description: Maximum width in pixels; pass null to clear it

minHeight.description: Minimum height in pixels; pass null to clear it

minWidth.description: Minimum width in pixels; pass null to clear it

nodeIds.description: Frame, component, component set, or instance node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345', '4029:67890']

primaryAxisAlignItems.description: Main-axis alignment: MIN, CENTER, MAX, or SPACE_BETWEEN

strokesIncludedInLayout.description: Count this node's stroke width as part of the layout size

set_auto_layout.name: set_auto_layout

set_codegen_result.description: Attach generated code to a node so it appears in Figma's Dev Mode Code panel. This is how code you write with the repository in front of you reaches the designers: it is stored in the file, so every teammate's Dev Mode shows it, not just this machine. Dev Mode looks at the node itself, then at the component an instance came from, then at its ancestors — so putting the code on a component covers every instance of it. Pass an empty blocks array to remove what is stored.

blocks.description: Code blocks to show, one tab each. Empty removes the stored code.

language.description: Syntax highlighting: TYPESCRIPT, JAVASCRIPT, HTML, CSS, JSON, GRAPHQL, PYTHON, GO, SQL, SWIFT, KOTLIN, RUBY, CPP, RUST, BASH, or PLAINTEXT. Anything else falls back to PLAINTEXT.

nodeId.description: Node ID to attach the code to, colon format e.g. '4029:12345'. A COMPONENT or COMPONENT_SET covers all its instances.

set_codegen_result.name: set_codegen_result

set_effects.description: Apply one or more effects directly to a node. Replaces all existing effects. Pass an empty array to clear all effects. The shape matches what get_nodes_info reports under styles.effects, so effects can be read off one node and written to another unchanged.

effects.description: Array of effect objects, each keyed by `type`. DROP_SHADOW / INNER_SHADOW: color (hex), opacity (0–1 colour alpha), offsetX, offsetY, radius, spread, blendMode; showShadowBehindNode on drop shadows. LAYER_BLUR / BACKGROUND_BLUR: radius; blurType PROGRESSIVE adds startRadius, startOffset, endOffset as {x, y}. NOISE: noiseType (MONOTONE default | DUOTONE | MULTITONE), color, opacity, blendMode, noiseSize, density; secondaryColor for DUOTONE, noiseOpacity for MULTITONE. TEXTURE: noiseSize, radius, clipToShape. GLASS: radius, depth, lightIntensity, lightAngle, refraction, dispersion. visible defaults to true on every type.

nodeId.description: Target node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

set_effects.name: set_effects

set_export_settings.description: Set the export presets on nodes — the entries a designer sees under Export in the right-hand panel, and what a Figma export or a handoff pipeline uses. This changes the document; it does not export anything. Use get_screenshot or save_screenshots to actually produce a file.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

settings.description: Export presets, in the order they should appear. An empty array clears the node's presets.

constraint.description: Raster size: {type: SCALE|WIDTH|HEIGHT, value}. SCALE 2 is @2x; WIDTH 512 fixes the width. Ignored for SVG and PDF.

contentsOnly.description: Exclude overlapping content outside the node (default true)

suffix.description: Appended to the file name, e.g. '@2x' or '-dark'

useAbsoluteBounds.description: Export the full node bounds even when it is clipped by its parent

set_export_settings.name: set_export_settings

set_instance_overrides.description: Update Component Properties (variants, booleans, text) on a component instance. Will fail-fast if property name or type is invalid.

nodeId.description: INSTANCE node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

properties.description: Map of property name to its new value. Example: {"Size": "Large", "Show Icon": true}

set_instance_overrides.name: set_instance_overrides

set_layout_grids.description: Set the layout grids drawn over a frame — columns, rows, or a square grid. These are the guides a layout is built against, distinct from a saved grid style. Pass an empty grids array to remove the grids a frame already has.

grids.description: Grids to draw. Empty removes every grid on the node.

alignment.description: COLUMNS/ROWS: how they sit in the frame (default STRETCH)

visible.description: Whether the grid is shown (default true)

mode.description: replace swaps the node's grids for these (default); append adds them

nodeIds.description: Frame, component, or section node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

set_layout_grids.name: set_layout_grids

set_node_properties.description: Set one or more properties on nodes in a single call: position, size, corner radius, visibility, lock state, opacity, rotation, blend mode, constraints, z-order, masking, and stroke geometry. Every property is optional and independent — supply only the ones you want to change. Each node reports which properties were applied; a property the node type does not support is reported against that property alone, leaving the others applied. Moving and resizing in one call is one undo entry, not two.

blendMode.description: Blend mode e.g. NORMAL, MULTIPLY, SCREEN, OVERLAY, LUMINOSITY

constraints.description: Responsive constraints {horizontal, vertical}, each MIN, MAX, CENTER, STRETCH, or SCALE. Axes you omit keep their current value.

cornerRadius.description: Uniform corner radius applied to all four corners

dashPattern.description: Dash lengths in pixels, alternating dash and gap e.g. [4, 2]. An empty array makes the stroke solid again.

height.description: New height in pixels. The width is left as it is unless you also pass width.

isMask.description: Turn the node into a mask for its later siblings (true) or back into an ordinary layer (false)

locked.description: Lock (true) or unlock (false) the nodes against accidental edits

maskType.description: How the mask is read: ALPHA uses opacity, VECTOR the outline, LUMINANCE the brightness

nodeIds.description: Node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

order.description: Change z-order: bringToFront, sendToBack, bringForward, or sendBackward

strokeAlign.description: Where the stroke sits relative to the shape's edge

strokeCap.description: How open ends are drawn: NONE, ROUND, SQUARE, or an arrowhead (ARROW_LINES, ARROW_EQUILATERAL). Applies to lines and open vector paths.

strokeJoin.description: How corners between segments are drawn

strokeMiterLimit.description: How far a MITER join may extend before it is bevelled instead (default 4)

strokeWeight.description: Stroke thickness in pixels. set_paint also takes this when it paints a stroke; use this one to change the thickness without repainting.

width.description: New width in pixels. The height is left as it is unless you also pass height.

x.description: Absolute X position on the canvas, applied to every node listed — not a relative offset from where each one is now

y.description: Absolute Y position on the canvas, applied to every node listed — not a relative offset from where each one is now

set_node_properties.name: set_node_properties

set_paint.description: Paint a node's fill or stroke. `type` selects the kind of paint and each takes its own arguments — SOLID: color, opacity. GRADIENT_LINEAR / GRADIENT_RADIAL: stops, geometry, opacity. `target` chooses fill (default) or stroke; gradients can only target fill. An argument belonging to a different kind is rejected rather than ignored.

color.description: SOLID: color as hex — #RRGGBB e.g. #FF5733, or #RRGGBBAA e.g. #FF573380 for 50% alpha (required)

geometry.description: GRADIENT: coordinates in percentX/Y — start, end, angle for linear; center, radius, rotation for radial (required)

mode.description: 'replace' (default) overwrites the existing paints; 'append' stacks this one on top

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

opacity.description: Paint opacity 0–1 (default 1). For SOLID it combines multiplicatively with any alpha in the color hex; for gradients it scales the whole gradient.

stops.description: GRADIENT: array of color stops e.g. [{position: 0, color: '#ff0000'}, {position: 1, color: '#00ff00'}] (required)

strokeWeight.description: Stroke weight in pixels (default 1). Only when target is stroke.

type.description: Kind of paint: SOLID, GRADIENT_LINEAR, or GRADIENT_RADIAL

set_paint.name: set_paint

mode.description: "replace" (default) overwrites all existing reactions; "append" adds to them

nodeId.description: Node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

reactions.description: Array of reaction objects. Each has a 'trigger' and an 'actions' array (plural) of Action objects.

set_reactions.name: set_reactions

set_selection.description: Select nodes in Figma and scroll the viewport to them, switching pages if needed. Use this to show the user what you just created or changed, or to point at the nodes a question is about. Pass no node IDs to clear the selection. All nodes must be on the same page — a Figma selection cannot span pages.

nodeIds.description: Node IDs to select in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']; omit or pass an empty list to clear the selection

select.description: Change the selection (default true). Pass false with zoom to move the camera without disturbing what the user has selected.

zoom.description: Scroll and zoom the viewport to fit the nodes (default true)

set_selection.name: set_selection

set_text.description: Update the text content of an existing TEXT node, and the settings that apply to the node as a whole — wrapping, truncation, alignment, and paragraph spacing. For styling that varies across the text (a bold word, a link, a bulleted list), use set_text_ranges.

maxLines.description: Cap the text at this many lines (needs textTruncation ENDING); pass null to remove the cap

nodeId.description: TEXT node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

textAlignVertical.description: Vertical text alignment within the box

textAutoResize.description: How the box sizes to its text: NONE (fixed), HEIGHT (grow down), WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT (hug), or TRUNCATE

textTruncation.description: ENDING adds an ellipsis when the text overflows

set_text.name: set_text

set_text_ranges.description: Style parts of a TEXT node independently: a bold word, a coloured phrase, a hyperlink, a bulleted list. Each range is a half-open character span [start, end) over the node's existing text, so call set_text first to put the text there. Ranges may overlap; they are applied in text order, so a later one wins where they meet. Omit a property to leave it as it is.

nodeId.description: TEXT node ID in colon format e.g. '4029:12345'

ranges.description: Character ranges to style. Each needs start and end; every other property is optional.

end.description: One past the last character index

fontFamily.description: Font family e.g. 'Inter'. With fontStyle omitted, the range keeps its current style.

fontStyle.description: Font style e.g. 'Bold', 'Italic'. With fontFamily omitted, the range keeps its current family.

hyperlink.description: URL to link the range to; pass null to remove an existing link

lineHeight.description: Line height as a number, or the string 'AUTO'

lineHeightUnit.description: Unit for a numeric lineHeight (default PIXELS)

listType.description: Turn the range into a numbered or bulleted list

set_text_ranges.name: set_text_ranges

set_variable_value.description: Set a variable's value for a specific mode.

value.description: Value to set. COLOR: hex e.g. #FF5733. FLOAT: number e.g. 16. STRING: text. BOOLEAN: true or false.

set_variable_value.name: set_variable_value

swap_component.description: Swap the main component of an existing INSTANCE node, replacing it with a different component while keeping position and size.

componentId.description: Target COMPONENT node ID in colon format (from get_local_components)

nodeId.description: INSTANCE node ID in colon format e.g. 4029:12345

swap_component.name: swap_component

ungroup_nodes.description: Ungroup one or more GROUP nodes, moving their children to the parent and removing the group.

nodeIds.description: GROUP node IDs in colon format e.g. ['4029:12345']

ungroup_nodes.name: ungroup_nodes

update_paint_style.description: Update an existing paint style's name, color, or description. Only paint styles support in-place updates — to modify text, effect, or grid styles, use delete_style and recreate them.

color.description: New fill color as hex e.g. #FF5733

update_paint_style.name: update_paint_style
